_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.good_example: Public Profile görünen adında aşırı şekilli yazı veya emoji kullanmak arama sonuçlarında görünürlüğünü azaltabilir.

phrases.usage_guidance: Useful as a criteria checklist inside a future 'klan ismi nasıl seçilir' section on tr/usecase/coc-nick or a dedicated answers page.
phrases.good_example: Türkçe ve Yabancı Clan İsimleri: Anlamlı, Akılda Kalıcı ve Benzersiz

phrases.register: formal/dated — still used in banking/legal contexts and older forum culture; 'nick' now dominates casual/gaming speech
phrases.usage_guidance: Do not lead copy with 'rumuz' for a gaming/social audience — it reads dated. Fine as a secondary/glossary synonym for 'nick' or 'takma isim' if targeting an older or more formal search query.
phrases.good_example: Mahlas / Rumuz / Nick Danışması
phrases.avoid_when: targeting Gen Z gaming audience as the primary term

phrases.usage_guidance: Useful as an adjacent context word when writing bio/profile-styling copy ('bio'nu ve pp'ni güncelle') but not a text-styling term itself — low priority for a page title.
phrases.good_example: Pp Ne Demek? Sosyal Medyada Kullanılan Pp Kelimesinin Türkçe Anlamı Nedir?

phrases.content_surface: n/a — not present in repo, but relevant to UTG's own value proposition of clean client-side Unicode output
phrases.usage_guidance: Reassurance copy opportunity: UTG's client-side rendering doesn't mangle Turkish diacritics the way some copy-paste workflows do — could anchor a trust-building FAQ line.
phrases.good_example: PDF üzerindeki yazıları Word'de kopyala yapıştır yaptığımda karakterler okunamaz hale geliyor.

phrases.usage_guidance: 'Ay yıldız' is the colloquial term Turkish speakers actually use and search for this symbol; the more formal 'hilal ve yıldız' is understood but is not the phrase people type. Lead with 'ay yıldız' in the title/H1/meta and keep 'hilal ve yıldız' alongside it rather than deleting it — both are correct and the page should read naturally for both. Register note, confirmed against two independent native sources: 'ay yıldız' is framed around the flag and national identity, while 'hilal' is the word natives use for the religious/Islamic reading of the crescent.
phrases.good_example: Ay Yıldız Sembolü: Kopyala Yapıştır ☪
phrases.avoid_when: Do not swap 'ay yıldız' in where the copy is specifically discussing the crescent as a religious/Islamic symbol (e.g. the page's own 'not a symbol found in the Quran' section) — 'hilal' is the correct word there, and native forum usage keeps the two distinct ('hilal islamiyet, yıldız da türklüğü simgeliyor'). Keep both words on the page, each in its own context.

phrases.content_surface: title/H1/meta on a nazar/evil-eye symbol page
phrases.usage_guidance: Lead with the full head-term 'nazar boncuğu' in the title/H1/meta of a Turkish evil-eye page, and keep 'nazar sembolleri' alongside it — both are correct and each has its own demand. First-party GSC confirms Turks type the full phrase: the only nazar query drawing impressions for this site is 'nazar boncuğu emoji kombinasyonları', never bare 'nazar'. Bare 'nazar' stays the right word inside running prose, where repeating the full phrase reads unnatural.
phrases.good_example: Nazar Boncuğu Sembolü 🧿 Kopyala Yapıştır
phrases.avoid_when: Do not replace every occurrence of 'nazar' with 'nazar boncuğu' — 'nazar' alone is the correct word for the CONCEPT (the evil eye / the gaze itself), while 'nazar boncuğu' names the physical bead/amulet. Body prose discussing the belief should keep 'nazar'; the targeting layer and the sections about the object should use 'nazar boncuğu'.

phrases.content_surface: candidate secondary H2/FAQ term on tr/usecase/pubg-nick/ — not title/H1 ("PUBG" itself stays primary; this is a colloquial variant, not the dominant search term)
phrases.usage_guidance: Confirmed 2026-07-31: "papçı"/"papci" refers to the GAME ITSELF (a Turkish phonetic respelling of "PUBG"), not to a player of it — corrects this record's original guess. Directly-fetched evidence: a Cenuta blog post states "Papci olarak okunan PUBG'yi oynayabilmek için..." ("To be able to play PUBG, read as Papci..."), and a complaints-site page titles itself "PUBG (Pubgmobile.com) Papçi Oyunu Zararları" ("the Papçi game"), both using it as a name for the game, not the player. Safe as a secondary/FAQ synonym for "PUBG" on pubg-nick (e.g. "...also written 'papçı' by some players"), not as a replacement for "PUBG" in title/H1.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use as the primary term in title/H1/meta — "PUBG" is the dominant, SEO-correct term; "papçı" is a colloquial variant worth a secondary mention only.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'çalışma sayfası' for a tracing/handwriting generator's output (it is drill-shaped) and reserve 'etkinlik' for craft/cut-out outputs. Pair with 'ücretsiz' and 'PDF indir' — Turkish resource searches carry both.
phrases.good_example: Harf çalışma sayfaları — ücretsiz PDF indir ve yazdır.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'çalışma kağıdı' as the head term (attested, but 'sayfa' dominates on the resource sites). Do not label a purely decorative colouring sheet a 'çalışma sayfası' — Turkish parents read that as practice work, and the colouring word is separate (see P41).

phrases.usage_guidance: This is the best-evidenced tr formulation for the printable-outline-letters job, and the site has no Turkish printables cluster at all — so it is a vocabulary finding for whenever one is scoped. Pair with 'A4' and 'PDF', which Turkish resource pages state explicitly.
phrases.good_example: Alfabe harf kalıpları — tek tek harfleri A4 ebatında PDF olarak indirebilirsiniz.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'kalıp' for on-screen Unicode letters — it implies a physical cut-out/trace-around template. Do not use it where the sheet's job is handwriting practice on lines; that is a 'çalışma sayfası' (P39).

phrases.native_phrase: bitişik eğik yazı / dik temel harfler
phrases.english_concept: the named handwriting script Turkish first-graders are taught (and the 2019 change)
phrases.register: neutral, official/pedagogical — but the confusion is fully parent-facing
phrases.usage_guidance: The strongest Turkish finding for a handwriting-sheet cluster: a tr page must name which script it generates, because Turkish parents have lived through the switch and the two scripts look nothing alike. Use both names as selector labels, and use the change itself as an FAQ ('Hangi yazı öğretiliyor?'). Do not present 'el yazısı' alone as sufficient — that is the generic umbrella (TR-009).
phrases.good_example: Yazı türünü seç: bitişik eğik yazı veya dik temel harfler.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not state the current curriculum position as settled fact without re-checking the MEB source — curricula change, and this record is a vocabulary finding, not a live policy citation. Do not use these names for decorative/Unicode cursive styling: TR-009 ('el yazısı fontu') already covers that sense and these are handwriting models, not copy-paste fonts.

phrases.english_concept: a lettering/script tattoo (the category and the thing itself)
phrases.register: neutral — shared studio and customer vocabulary
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the thing being made; keep 'dövme yazı fontları' (TR-017) as the tool/page head term. Pairs naturally with 'isim dövmesi' (P15) for the name-tattoo section.
phrases.good_example: Yazı dövmeleri yaptırmayı düşünüyorsanız, önce fontu kendi isminizde deneyin.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use it where the user is picking a typeface — that is 'font' / 'yazı tipi'. Not applicable outside tattoo context.

phrases.native_phrase: isim dövmesi (ı ğ ş ç sorunu)
phrases.transliteration: isim dovmesi (i g s c sorunu)
phrases.english_concept: name tattoo — and the Turkish-character risk specific to it
phrases.register: neutral-technical when a studio says it; frustrated/worried when a customer does
phrases.usage_guidance: This is the single highest-value Turkish angle for the tattoo page: an FAQ heading in the user's own framing — does the style keep ı, ğ, ş, ç? — that most competitors do not answer. It supports the existing head term, it does not replace it. Mirror the honest caveat the German page already ships: the preview is a starting point and the artist draws the final letterform.
phrases.good_example: İsim dövmesinde ı, ğ, ş ve ç harfleri fontta bozuluyorsa, dövmecin o harfleri elle çizecek — önce kendi isminle test et.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not promise the tool 'fixes' Turkish characters — most Unicode style ranges genuinely have no styled glyph for ğ/ş/ı, and the honest answer is that they fall back to the plain letter. Do not use the frustrated register ('bozuluyor') in a title/H1; keep it in FAQ/body.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use to name the thin/delicate style option. Keep the English words untranslated — the Turkish suffix is what naturalises it.
phrases.good_example: El yazısı fontlar, fine line tekniğiyle ince versiyonlarda çok tercih ediliyor.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not translate it ('ince çizgi tekniği' is a description, not the style name). Do not use it to mean 'small'.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the heading for the date-conversion section of the tr tattoo page. A locally-observed caveat worth writing into the FAQ: high years get long in Roman numerals (1999 becomes MCMXCIX), which changes placement — that framing came from a Turkish studio, not from English sources.
phrases.good_example: Roma rakamlı tarih dövmesi klasik durur; ama 1999 → MCMXCIX gibi uzun çıkabilir, yerleşimi ona göre seç.
phrases.avoid_when: n/a as a term; do not build a separate Turkish page for it — it is a section of the tattoo page.

phrases.english_concept: writing lines stacked one below another in a bio (the Turkish framing of stacked text)
phrases.usage_guidance: Head term for a Turkish stacked-text page: 'alt alta yazma'. Use 'satır atlama' as the FAQ heading for the how-do-I-get-a-line-break step. Mention 'dikey' at most once, in body copy, for users arriving from tool documentation — do not put it in the H1.
phrases.good_example: Instagram biyografi alt alta yazma: yazını alt alta diz, kopyala ve biyografine yapıştır.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'dikey yazı' as the primary term for the social/decorative job — it skews to Word/Excel/CSS intent and will pull the wrong traffic. Do not use for the ja/ko writing-mode sense.

phrases.english_concept: 'what does this emoji mean' — the Turkish head phrasing (no native word for emoji)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'emoji anlamları' as the Turkish H1/title pattern, and let the sub-headings use the '… ne demek' question form which matches how Turkish users phrase it out loud. Turkish emoji pages in the wild are grouped by category (yüz / kalp / el işaretleri / hayvan emojileri) — mirroring that grouping matches reader expectation.
phrases.good_example: Emoji anlamları: WhatsApp ve Instagram'da en çok kullanılan yüz, kalp ve el işaretleri emojilerinin anlamları.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not invent a Turkish native noun for emoji ('duygu simgesi', 'ifade simgesi') — those are dictionary constructions with no observed search usage and will read as machine translation. Do not use 'emoji anlamları' on a copy-paste tool page; it promises a meaning reference.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'ASCII sanatı' in the H1 with the Latin 'ASCII art' in the same title/meta — Turkish users type both. 'Karakterlerle yapılan resimler' is the plain-Turkish description for the subheading.
phrases.good_example: ASCII sanatı (ASCII art): sadece klavye karakterleriyle yapılan, kopyalayıp yapıştırabileceğin resimler.
phrases.avoid_when: Not for single face emoticons. Avoid in gaming-nickname copy, where TR-001 'şekilli' register governs.

phrases.english_concept: text emoticon — and the Turkish terminology vacuum for kaomoji
phrases.content_surface: faq, body gloss only — NOT the H1
phrases.usage_guidance: A Turkish kaomoji page should NOT be titled 'ifade simgesi'. Lead with what Turks type — 'emoji'/'emoticon' plus the visible example characters and 'kopyala yapıştır' — and use 'ifade simgesi' once as the formal gloss. Because Turkish lacks a kaomoji word entirely, the page must carry the sideways-vs-upright explanation itself; there is no existing Turkish framing to borrow, unlike Indonesian's 'gaya Barat/Timur' or Dutch's quarter-turn image.
phrases.good_example: Bu ifade simgeleri (kaomoji) düz durur: ':-)' gibi yan yatmaz, başını yana eğmene gerek kalmaz.
phrases.avoid_when: Never use 'sındamga' anywhere — it is an academic coinage with effectively zero usage and its appearance would flag the page as machine-generated or pedantic. Avoid 'ifade simgesi' in casual/gaming copy.

phrases.english_concept: wedding invitation and the calligraphy service around it
phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'yazı tipi' (already the site's Turkish head word, cf. TR-018) with 'davetiye' as the qualifier. Supports an existing el yazısı/kaligrafi surface; not a page to build.
phrases.good_example: Davetli isimlerinin zarfın üzerine kaligrafi ile yazılması, davetiyeye ayrı bir zarafet katıyor.
phrases.avoid_when: Never on gaming/nickname pages. Do not promise a printable or hand-written result — 'davetiye yazımı' specifically means human hand-writing, and using it for a Unicode tool would be a false claim.

phrases.usage_guidance: Write 'başlık (headline)' on first mention, matching Turkish convention. Qualify as 'profil başlığı' where bare 'başlık' would be ambiguous with a page/article heading.
phrases.good_example: Özelleştirilmiş ve kişiselleştirilmiş bir başlık ile ayırt edilmenizi sağlayabilir.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use any TR gaming/decoration vocabulary here — TR-001 (şekilli nick), TR-014 (çerçeveli isim), TR-023 (aşırı şekilli yazı) belong to a completely different register and audience. TR-027 (rumuz) is formal but dated and means a pseudonym, not a headline.

phrases.usage_guidance: Use 'özet bölümü'; note that LinkedIn's Turkish UI may show 'Hakkında', so gloss it if the copy instructs the reader to click something.
phrases.good_example: Özet bölümü yetkinliklerinizi ve güçlü yönlerinizi öne çıkarmalı.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use TR-018's casual 'bio' here — that record is explicitly split between the formal 'biyografi' and the casual 'bio', and neither is the LinkedIn summary. Do not use gaming vocabulary.

phrases.register: neutral, everyday — the unmarked spoken/typed word
phrases.usage_guidance: 'Tik işareti' is the colloquial term Turkish speakers actually search for the ✓/✔/☑ glyph; 'onay işareti' is the formal register. Lead with 'tik işareti' in the title/H1 and keep 'onay işareti' as a secondary/synonym term on the same page — do not delete it, it has its own real demand and is the right word in approval/confirmation contexts.
phrases.good_example: Tik İşareti ✓ Kopyala Yapıştır — Onay İşareti ve Çarpı Sembolleri
phrases.avoid_when: Do not replace 'onay işareti' wholesale. Where the copy means approval/confirmation as an act (a form being approved, a verified badge), 'onay işareti' is the more precise word; 'tik işareti' names the glyph shape.

phrases.english_concept: Turkish letters shrink SMS from 160 to 70 chars (double billing)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in an SMS-mode FAQ: 'Türkçe karakterler neden SMS'i kısaltıyor?'. National-scale grievance (BTK intervened 2008; ekşi: 'turkcell'in türkçe karakter uyanıklığı').
Good tattoo-lettering page angle — sharper intent than generic 'yazı stilleri'.
Important for a TR heart-emoji-meaning page: an EN-parent page framed only around nature/luck would miss this locale-distinct sense.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not state jealousy as the ONLY meaning — nature/environment sense also applies.

phrases.native_phrase: klan etiketi / lonca tag / takım etiketi
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for Discord clan-tag content; 'lonca' (guild) is used colloquially/interchangeably with 'klan'/'takım'.
Flavor/example use only — too colloquial for title/H1/meta.
phrases.avoid_when: Formal or technical copy.
